content.title: About
content.content: Baked chicken wings coated with a crispy breading are a popular snack alternative. They are cooked without added oil, making them less fatty, while the coating provides a flavorful, crunchy crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baked wings retain most of their protein but contain less fat than deep‑fried versions.
The coating is often a mix of flour, spices, and breadcrumbs, allowing flavors from classic paprika to hot chili.
Wings are a traditional appetizer in the United States, commonly served with blue‑cheese or ranch dressing.
Typical baking temperature is 200‑220 °C, which creates an even golden crust.
Chicken wings are rich in collagen, which may support joint and skin health.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken wings provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Lower fat when baked
items.content: Baking without added oil reduces saturated fat compared with frying.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Wings contain vitamins B6 and B12, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Chicken meat is a good source of iron, zinc, and selenium, important for immune health.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Phosphorus in wings contributes to strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Sodium in breading
items.content: Pre‑made coating mixes often contain salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Risk of undercooking
items.content: Chicken must reach an internal temperature of 74 °C to prevent foodborne illness.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Even baked, wings can be calorie‑dense, especially with a thick coating, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a snack with sauces such as barbecue, ranch, or blue‑cheese. They can be added to salads, used in tacos, or enjoyed straight from the plate. For a lighter option, choose a coating without added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked baked wings in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: Muffin Oat Bran is a blend of whole oat flakes, oat bran, dried fruit and nuts designed for a quick, nutritious breakfast. The product is high in fiber, B‑vitamins and minerals, and provides slowly digestible carbohydrates for lasting satiety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat bran is one of the richest sources of soluble and insoluble fiber.
Dried fruit adds natural sweetness without added sugar.
Oat‑based cereals are popular in sports nutrition for their carbohydrate and protein content.
Bran helps regulate blood cholesterol levels.
The product is ready in minutes – just add hot water or milk.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the bran stimulates intestinal motility and promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Lowers cholesterol
items.content: Beta‑glucans in oats can reduce cholesterol absorption in the gut.

items.title: Sustained energy source
items.content: Complex carbs release slowly, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B6 and folate aid carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Minerals for bones and muscles
items.content: Magnesium, iron and zinc contribute to normal muscle and bone function.

items.title: Gluten sensitivity
items.content: Oats can be cross‑contaminated with wheat; people with celiac disease should choose certified gluten‑free oats.

items.title: High fiber content
items.content: A sudden increase may cause bloating or abdominal discomfort.

items.title: Natural sugar in dried fruit
items.content: Those monitoring blood sugar should account for the fruit’s natural sugars.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour hot water or milk over the cereal and let it sit for 3–5 minutes. Add yogurt, nuts, seeds or fresh berries for extra flavor and texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to preserve crunchiness.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato French Fries NFS (4216) are thin strips of potato that are deep‑fried until golden and crisp. The product is made from selected varieties of potatoes that are blanched, dried and lightly coated with vegetable oil before frying. The fries have a crunchy exterior and a soft, aromatic interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “fries” comes from the English word “fried”.
French fries first appeared in the United States in the early 1920s as a street snack.
There are more than 30 cutting styles for fries: classic, steak, curly, waffle, etc.
In 2015 NFS launched a production line that can produce fries with less than 10 % fat.
Fries are commonly served with sauces such as ketchup, mayonnaise, cheese sauce, and barbecue.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potatoes contain vitamin C, an antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in potatoes aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: French fries provide complex carbs that serve as an energy source.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: Yellow and orange potatoes contain beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds a significant amount of fat, increasing the calorie density.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Fries are often salted; excessive sodium intake can affect blood pressure.

items.title: Acrylamide
items.content: Cooking at very high temperatures can form acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a side dish or a snack. Sprinkle with salt, spices, cheese powder, or dip in various sauces. For a healthier option, bake or air‑fry the fries instead of deep‑frying.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen fries in an airtight bag at –18 °C. Once thawed, cook immediately to preserve quality. Cooked fries should be consumed within 2 hours at room temperature.
